review_notes: I read the whole file. I searched Mathlib for other definitions named toList, toCycle and formPerm, and for every use of isoCycle and isoCycle'. Cycle.formPerm lifts List.formPerm (Mathlib/GroupTheory/Perm/List.lean) to quotients, so it is not a competing concept. Perm.toList and Perm.toCycle have no Mathlib counterpart. The Repr instance and the c[...] notation are new and have no counterpart either. The only duplication I found is isoCycle versus isoCycle'. I am only moderately confident in it, because the docstrings present the two as deliberate alternative implementations. A grep over the Mathlib directory found no use of either name outside this file.

findings.excerpt: def isoCycle' : { f : Perm α // IsCycle f } ≃ { s : Cycle α // s.Nodup ∧ s.Nontrivial } :=
findings.problem: The file defines the same equivalence twice. `isoCycle` and `isoCycle'` have identical types and identical `invFun` (`Cycle.formPerm`). They differ only in how the forward map is computed: `toCycle` in one, `Fintype.bijInv` over the uniqueness lemma in the other. The module docstring admits 'It is unclear if this works faster than the `Equiv.Perm.toCycle`', so the second version has no demonstrated benefit. Neither name is used anywhere else in Mathlib. Anyone choosing between them gets two propositionally equal but not syntactically equal equivalences, and there is no lemma relating them.
findings.proposed_change: Keep only `isoCycle`, which is computable through `toCycle` and has the useful `toCycle_eq_toList` API. Delete `isoCycle'` and its docstring and module-doc entries. If both are kept, add a lemma `isoCycle' = isoCycle` (provable from `existsUnique_cycle_nontrivial_subtype`) and say in the docstring why both exist.
findings.benefit: This removes a second, unused definition of the same bijection and the unresolved performance remark. It also removes the risk of the two versions diverging, and it gives readers one canonical equivalence between cyclic permutations and nodup nontrivial cycles.
